_meta.indication: OLYSIO is an HCV NS3/4A protease inhibitor indicated for the treatment of chronic hepatitis C (CHC) infection as a component of a combination antiviral treatment regimen; efficacy established in combination with peginterferon alfa and ribavirin in HCV genotype 1 infected subjects with compensated liver disease (including cirrhosis)

pivotal_trials.trial_name: QUEST 1 (study C208) and QUEST 2 (study C216), pooled treatment-naive Phase 3 trials
pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed FDA documents
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 2-arm, multicenter superiority trials: 12 weeks of once-daily 150 mg OLYSIO or placebo plus Peg-IFN-alfa-2a (QUEST 1 and QUEST 2) or Peg-IFN-alfa-2b (QUEST 2) and RBV, followed by 12 or 36 weeks of Peg-IFN-alfa and RBV per response-guided therapy (controls received 48 weeks of Peg-IFN-alfa-2a or -2b and RBV)
pivotal_trials.population: Treatment-naive adults with chronic HCV genotype 1 infection with compensated liver disease (including cirrhosis)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: SVR12 (HCV RNA lower than 25 IU/mL detectable or undetectable 12 weeks after the planned end of treatment)

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed FDA documents
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 2-arm, multicenter trial: 12 weeks of once-daily 150 mg OLYSIO or placebo plus Peg-IFN-alfa-2a and RBV, followed by 12 or 36 weeks of Peg-IFN-alfa-2a and RBV per response-guided criteria (control received 48 weeks of Peg-IFN-alfa-2a and RBV)
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with chronic HCV genotype 1 infection who relapsed after prior interferon-based therapy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: SVR12 (HCV RNA lower than 25 IU/mL detectable or undetectable 12 weeks after the planned end of treatment)

nct_ctgov.title: An Efficacy, Safety and Tolerability Study of TMC435 in Genotype 1 Hepatitis C-infected Patients Who Relapsed After Previous Therapy

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>20%) occurring at least 3% more often than placebo were rash (including photosensitivity), pruritus and nausea. In the AE table (first 12 weeks): rash 28% vs 20% placebo, pruritus 22% vs 15%, nausea 22% vs 18%. Serious photosensitivity reactions resulting in hospitalization were observed.
target_moa: Simeprevir is an inhibitor of the HCV NS3/4A protease, which is essential for viral replication

rems.type: DAVP and DRISK agreed that no REMS is needed; primary safety risks (rash and hypersensitivity) can be addressed in professional labeling

companion_dx_detail: No companion diagnostic was required; FDA strongly recommends screening HCV genotype 1a patients for the NS3 Q80K polymorphism but determined the test was not 'essential'

advisory_committee.vote: The Antiviral Drugs Advisory Committee convened October 24, 2013 and voted unanimously (19 voting members) for approval of simeprevir

basis.text: The simeprevir NDA was given a priority review

citations.quote: The simeprevir NDA was given a priority review and presented before an advisory committee meeting as discussed below.

summary.text: The simeprevir NDA received a priority review and was presented before the Antiviral Drugs Advisory Committee, which voted unanimously for approval. Although the primary endpoint (SVR12) is a virologic measurement, FDA considers it clinically validated, so the approval was a traditional (not accelerated) approval.

citations.quote: The simeprevir NDA was given a priority review and presented before an advisory committee meeting as discussed below. Although the primary endpoint used in the phase 3 trials is a virologic measurement (undetectable virus twelve weeks after the end of therapy, referred to as SVR12), FDA considers this endpoint clinically validated. Therefore approvals using this endpoint will not fall under accelerated approval regulations. The expected regulatory action will be traditional approval. The SVR endpoint has been used in several prior approvals for the treatment of chronic hepatitis C including pegylated interferon plus ribavirin, boceprevir, and telaprevir.
the AC voted unanimously (19 voting members) for the approval of simeprevir.
